messages.subject: Re: prob/distributions vs. agrad/distributions
parts:
I'm more concerned about the client-facing behavior
than how we code it (other than the encoding has to
be efficient because it's in a tight loop).

What do you propose the behavior is when a bounds
check fails? Does that include NaN checks?

I'd just convinced myself we could just go with
NaN returns and not even worry about raising exceptions
or other control-flow altering or logging behavior if
we follow the behavior of the built-in arithmetic
and std lib functions.

As to how it's coded, whatever seems most convenient
to you is how you should do it. I'd be happy to look
at the first function you fully code up and give
you feedback. I find it hard to make these kinds of
coding decisions without getting my hands dirty.

You might want to generalize the bool parameter
to an enum depending on the options for handling
errors.

The bounds check functions might not be so useful if
the work they need to do is returning NaN. In that
case, they'd actually have to be macros.

Multiple exit points are just easier to code and
easier to understand (in my opinion). I don't think
compute time's an issue, though having a local
variable isn't ideal for efficiency.

- Bob


On 11/10/11 1:29 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Yeah... sounds good. I haven't thought much about generation of the message.
>
> I like what you've suggested. Do you mind if I go forward with it? It being:
> - a bounds check method for each distribution
> - returns true or false (with multiple exit points so we don't have to
> sit there forever waiting)
> - templating the distribution functions with the bool parameter
> - the bounds check method would not return a smart message. That would
> still be handled by the distribution function.
>
> Does that sounds good?
>
>
> Daniel
